cells.tense: You are still moving through the dim stretch, and the motion itself is what you lean on now.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Shoulder one bill, repair, or reply that's yours and see it through alone — no piece handed off, no help asked.
cells.core:
You can keep walking a road whose end you can't see. Enough light for the next stretch, rarely the whole way, and you go by that much — when things get unclear past what you know, you keep to the pace you already set instead of stopping to invent a reason to move. Being tested hasn't broken it. It's gotten quieter, and more yours.

Shoulder one bill, repair, or reply that's yours and see it through alone — every piece of it, no passing off. Whatever holds you up when the weight lands is what's been under you, steady, without a name you'd give it. You don't have to solve the road to keep on it. Some of this season the footing stays as unsure as it ever was; you'll be moving while it does.

cells.tense: You will be braced for the next strain before it has arrived to be met.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Keep both readings of something unsettled alive in you at once, side by side, and hand down no verdict between them.
cells.core:
You keep to the path, and lately you're trying to keep to every version of it at once. All the ways the ground could give, held open, waiting to be sure of the next stretch before you take it — so the step keeps not getting taken while you brace. The staying-on has turned into grip. What's ahead gets re-read instead of walked.

Keep both readings of something unsettled alive in you at once, side by side, and hand down no verdict between them. A decision can rest on that; the grip cannot. It's when holding both stops being possible that the walk stalls — and stalling is what the grip costs where you are now.

cells.tense: You were headed somewhere once, and you are still standing at its edge.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Give one patch that's yours — a plant, a shelf — steady tending on the same days each week, long enough to watch it change.
cells.core:
The road ran out a while back, or the point you were headed for stopped being visible, and the walking stopped with it. You're at the edge of something that ended — the next move keeps not being made, the fuel you'd need for it not arriving. So the days churn and nothing you're building moves. The churning works in place of mileage; it has no destination.

Give one patch that's actually yours — a plant, a shelf — steady tending on the same days each week, long enough to watch it change shape in your hands. No project and no fix. That's how aim returns: something tended long enough to become different, which is the only way a road shows itself to somebody standing still.
cells.sheetLine: The churning is doing the work of walking.

cells.tense: You are steering through weather and calling it nothing you are doing.
cells.act: persist on your own reserves through the pressure
cells.ask: When strain lands, meet it on what you have and keep your hand on it — then mark, for yourself, whose strength saw it through.
cells.core:
You've kept to a direction through a long dim stretch, and if someone asked you'd say it's circumstance, or stubbornness, or nothing in particular. It keeps reading as habit. Meanwhile the going-on keeps happening, under no name at all — not deliberate, not chosen, not seen anywhere.

When strain lands, meet it on what you have and keep your own hand on it. Then mark, for yourself, whose strength saw it through; put your name on that. No annotation past the mark. It isn't a new decision. It's seeing the one you already made, and using the kind of strength that only works when you stand in it.
cells.sheetLine: Looking isn't habit, it's the oar.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that this persistence is still aimed at a star the person once chose — for all the record says, the ongoingness may be aimless momentum, old habit, or someone else's plan. A reader who lost their direction years ago could fairly say 'I'm not still following anything, I'm just still going.' The asks survive that being wrong: every one is small, bounded, and drawn from the medicine's own palette, so it teaches something (quarterly clearing, latitude, tending, or choosing a route) even if the read misses. The sentence that serves me more than the reader is the one about still following a chosen star after everything, since it casts whatever they have weathered as faith — cut it before it reaches the page.
